chains.title: Ref G allele preserves a TCF/LEF site bound by TCF7L2 in the 8q24 enhancer, supporting long-range Wnt-driven MYC activation
chains.element: ENCODE cCRE EH38E3858447 (pELS) / Ensembl enhancer ENSR8_CGMBX, chr8:127401053-127401303

links.claim: TCF7L2 is covered only through CIS-BP-mapped models of related HMG/Sox family members (LEF1, TCF7, TCF7L1, group G041). Two of these pass the gate with negative effects (LEF1 z -4.66, effect -0.47; TCF7 z -4.59, effect -0.229), i.e. the alt T allele binds less and the ref G allele binds more. I chose TCF7L2 within this shared TCF/LEF specificity because it is the family member with a ChIP-seq peak covering this exact position in HCT116 (ENCSR000EUV). Caveat: the effect sizes are small, the models rank only ~350/997 by |z|, and the per-model site-strength percentiles are not internally consistent (TCF7 model ref 96.9th vs alt 99.2th).

The variant lies in an accessible, H3K27ac-marked proximal enhancer-like cCRE (DNase z 5.2, H3K27ac z 4.8, maxima across biosamples, not HCT116-specific) that is also annotated as an Ensembl enhancer.

MYC is the nearest cancer-relevant protein-coding gene (334 kb upstream of the element). Cited evidence for this specific link is weak: Open Targets gives MYC only L2G 0.05 against POU5F1B 0.89, and no eQTL, Hi-C or CRISPR evidence for an element-MYC connection is in the record; a PVT1 single-cell eQTL in colon goblet cells (PIP 0.95) is the only MYC-region molecular QTL cited.
TCF7L2 occupies this position in HCT116, a colorectal line, by ENCODE ChIP-seq, so the relevant TF is present and bound in colorectal cells.

rs6983267 is among the strongest CRC signals (p 2e-122; several entries list G as the effect allele for colorectal cancer/advanced adenoma, colon polyps and benign colon neoplasm, while the top 2022 entry lists T). If G is the risk allele, more TCF7L2 binding on G raising MYC output fits; the inconsistent effect-allele reporting in the catalog is unresolved and weakens this link.

predictions: Allele-specific read counts in the existing HCT116 TCF7L2 ChIP (ENCSR000EUV) show excess G-allele reads at chr8:127401060.
4C/Capture-C from this element contacts the MYC promoter, and prime-edited G>T clones lower MYC mRNA without changing POU5F1B.
Wnt stimulation amplifies the G>T reporter difference.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP or EMSA shows no G preference or a T preference.
Single-base allele swap changes POU5F1B/CCAT2 but leaves MYC unchanged.

chains.title: Null: no TF-binding-mediated effect of this base itself (linked causal variant in the adjacent cCREs, or no allelic effect)
predictions: Prime-edited single-base G>T clones change neither MYC, POU5F1B, CCAT2 nor proliferation.
Allele-specific read counts in existing HCT116 ChIP data show balanced alleles at chr8:127401060.
Fine-mapping in further ancestries moves the signal to EH38E3858446/EH38E3858448; the GTEx POU5F1B signal is driven by a linked variant.
falsified_if: A single-base allelic replacement reproducibly changes enhancer activity or target-gene expression.
Any TF shows reproducible allele-specific occupancy at this position in colonic cells.

chains.title: Same TCF7L2 site, but the gene it controls is POU5F1B/CCAT2, not MYC: loss of TCF7L2 binding on the T allele raises POU5F1B in colon
chains.element: cCRE EH38E3858447 (pELS), overlapping the CCAT2 exon / CASC8 intron
chains.cell_type: Colon / colorectal adenocarcinoma cells (Colon_Transverse tissue; HCT 116)

links.claim: Identical binding evidence to H1: CIS-BP-mapped TCF/LEF models give a ref-preferring change (LEF1 effect -0.47, z -4.66; TCF7 effect -0.229, z -4.59), and TCF7L2 itself is chosen within this specificity group because an ENCODE TCF7L2 ChIP peak in HCT116 contains the variant.
The variant is an exonic base of CCAT2 inside an active proximal enhancer-like cCRE whose SCREEN-linked genes are CCAT2, PCAT1 and POU5F1B.

The alt T allele is associated with higher POU5F1B expression in Colon_Transverse (GTEx NES +0.20, p 8.2e-06) and with lower CASC8 in whole blood (NES -0.32); Open Targets L2G favours POU5F1B (0.89), and TWAS implicates POU5F1B at this locus. Direction is consistent with ref-G TCF7L2 binding acting repressively or with TCF7L2 loss permitting local transcription, but the repressive role itself is not demonstrated by any cited experiment.
The eQTL is measured in transverse colon, and TCF7L2 is bound at this position in the colorectal line HCT116, so TF and target respond in the same tissue.

POU5F1B promotes colorectal cancer cell proliferation and metastasis, so a T-allele increase in POU5F1B fits the top CRC association entry, in which T is the effect allele (p 2e-122); entries listing G as effect allele for related colon traits are not reconciled.

predictions: Prime-edited G>T clones in a colorectal line raise POU5F1B/CCAT2 with little or no change in MYC.
TCF7L2 knockdown raises POU5F1B in G/G but not T/T backgrounds.
Genotype-stratified colon RNA shows POU5F1B, not MYC, tracking the variant.
falsified_if: Allele swap changes MYC but not POU5F1B/CCAT2.
TCF7L2 depletion lowers rather than raises POU5F1B, i.e. the site acts as an activator of POU5F1B.

chains.title: Ref G allele supports ZBTB43 binding; loss on the T allele de-represses the local CCAT2/POU5F1B unit
chains.element: cCRE EH38E3858447, overlapping the CCAT2 exon / CASC8 intron

links.claim: QBiC has an own model for ZBTB43 (group G404, single member) with a ref-preferring effect (z -23.26, effect -1.724; ref 99.8th to alt 87.9th percentile), and ZBTB43 is expressed at 8.32 TPM in HCT 116. This is an in vitro prediction only; other expressed ref-preferring hits exist (e.g. MBNL2 at 26.09 TPM, an RNA-binding CCCH protein), so ZBTB43 is not uniquely indicated.
The variant is an exonic base of CCAT2 inside an active proximal enhancer-like cCRE; no cited evidence shows ZBTB43 occupancy or a repressive role there.

POU5F1B carries the highest L2G score at this locus (0.89), has TWAS support, and shows a colon eQTL in which the T allele raises expression (NES +0.20), the direction expected if a ref-bound repressor is lost.
ZBTB43 is expressed in HCT 116 (8.32 TPM) and POU5F1B is functional in colorectal cancer cells; no ChIP evidence places ZBTB43 at this element.
Higher POU5F1B promotes colorectal proliferation and metastasis, consistent with the T-allele CRC association in the top catalog entry; other entries list G as effect allele and are not reconciled.

predictions: ZBTB43 ChIP or EMSA shows G-preferential occupancy at chr8:127401060.
ZBTB43 depletion raises POU5F1B/CCAT2 only in G-allele-containing cells.
TCF7L2 depletion leaves the allelic effect intact.
falsified_if: ZBTB43 shows no binding at this sequence in cells.
Allelic effect persists after ZBTB43 knockout.

chains.title: Alt T allele strengthens a COUP-TF/ESRR-type nuclear-receptor site (group G002) read by an abundant family member such as NR2F2

links.claim: QBiC group G002 (nuclear receptor, 29 models) has an alt-preferring best model (NR2F6, own model, z 20.82, effect 1.92; ref 98.6th to alt 100.0th percentile), but passing members disagree in direction (NR2C2 z -6.01). NR2F2 is only a CIS-BP-mapped member of this shared specificity and is not itself a named passing member; it is chosen only because it is the most abundant covered member in HCT 116 (61.74 TPM), which is a weak basis. NR2F6 (37.02 TPM) is an equally plausible reader.
The site is in an accessible, H3K27ac-marked proximal enhancer-like cCRE (values are maxima over biosamples, not HCT116-specific).

The element's linked genes are CCAT2/PCAT1/POU5F1B, and the only colon eQTL for this variant is POU5F1B (alt T raises it), so POU5F1B is the target if the alt-preferring nuclear-receptor site acts as an activator.
NR2F2 and related receptors are highly expressed in this colorectal line, making occupancy possible; occupancy itself is not shown.
Higher POU5F1B promotes CRC cell growth and metastasis, matching a T-risk-allele reading of the association.

predictions: NR2F2 (or NR2F6) ChIP shows T-biased occupancy at the variant; knockdown reduces POU5F1B in T-allele cells.
Mutating the nuclear-receptor half-site, but not the TCF/LEF core, abolishes the allelic reporter difference.
falsified_if: No NR2F2/NR2F6 signal at this cCRE in colorectal cells.
Allelic reporter difference persists after disrupting the predicted NR half-site.

grades_v0.reason: No cited evidence addresses TCF7L2 at this variant. E01, E03 and E04 are annotation and GWAS only, and there is no QBiC model, ChIP or allele-specific assay. The claim is asserted from memory, and the chain gives no coverage check for TCF7L2.

E03 places the variant in pELS EH38E3858447 with DNase z 5.2 and H3K27ac z 4.8, and E01 gives the ENSR8_CGMBX enhancer. The z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not HCT 116 specific. The claim 'only plausible function' is over-stated.

E02 gives only distance (MYC 334 kb). E05 gives MYC an L2G of 0.05 against POU5F1B 0.89, so the evidence points away from MYC. There is no eQTL, Hi-C or CRISPR support for the enhancer-MYC link, and the claim cites the weak MYC L2G as support.
E04 and E06a say nothing about Wnt activity or TCF7L2 in colon or HCT 116. No expression or ChIP evidence for TCF7L2 was provided.

E04 supports a strong CRC association, but the effect allele is inconsistent across entries (T in the top CRC entry, G in others). The association does not show that MYC mediates it. The claim that G is the risk allele conflicts with the top entry (T), and the cited effect directions are not reconciled.

E08 shows an alt-preferring QBiC change for group G372 (z 53.69). The best model is NR2E1, which is not expressed (0 TPM). Picking HNF4A on expression grounds is a reasonable but unvalidated choice, because HNF4A has only a CIS-BP-mapped model. Expression is low (2.95 TPM), and this is a binding prediction alone.
E03 shows the variant lies in a pELS with high DNase and H3K27ac, though these are maxima over biosamples and do not show HCT 116 activity.
The claim that MYC is the only cancer-relevant protein-coding gene is unsupported. E05 favours POU5F1B (L2G 0.89) over MYC (0.05), which contradicts the target choice.

E08 gives HNF4A 2.95 TPM and HNF4G 2.24 TPM, which is low expression. Nothing cited shows these are expressed in intestinal epithelium, and the claim cites expression only in HCT 116 in E08. Tissue restriction is not shown.

E04 gives a T-allele CRC association in the top entry, but this does not link the effect to MYC or to HNF4A, and the effect allele is inconsistent across entries. Direction is nominally consistent (alt binds more and the T allele raises risk) only if HNF4A is activating.

E14 shows G002 with an alt-preferring best model (NR2F6), but members disagree on direction (NR2C2 is negative). Choosing NR2F2 on TPM alone is not justified. NR2F2 is not a listed passing member in the shown text, and E16 is a different group (G037), so it does not support this. The best model is also NR2F6, a different TF.
E03 shows an accessible, H3K27ac-marked pELS at the variant, though the values are maxima over biosamples.
The chain admits local annotation to CCAT2/PCAT1/POU5F1B and asserts MYC as the long-range target without evidence. E05 gives MYC an L2G of 0.05 against POU5F1B 0.89, which contradicts the claim.
E14 shows high expression of NR2F2 and other receptors in HCT 116, which makes occupancy possible, but occupancy is not shown.
E04 shows the CRC association only. The claimed direction is left ambiguous (the chain says the effect may be repressive), so the chain is not consistent about whether T raises or lowers MYC.

E12 shows a ref-preferring ZBTB43 own-model change (z -23.26) with 8.32 TPM expression. This is a binding prediction alone, and no ChIP or allele-specific assay supports it. The claim of 'highest expression among single-TF ref-preferring hits' is wrong, since MBNL2 is 26.09 TPM (E13).
E01 and E03 show the variant is in a CCAT2 exon and in an active cCRE, but nothing shows ZBTB43 acts as a repressor there. The repressor role is asserted from memory.

E05 gives POU5F1B an L2G of 0.89 and E06b a TWAS signal, which are genetic and expression support for the gene in general. They do not link this variant or element to POU5F1B through a perturbation or eQTL, and E06b does not mention the variant. CCAT2 is not supported by cited evidence.
E06c shows POU5F1B function in CRC cells, but no cited evidence shows POU5F1B expression in HCT 116 or that this variant acts there.

E06c supports POU5F1B promoting CRC cell proliferation and metastasis, and E04 supports the association. The direction is inconsistent: ref binds more and the T allele de-represses POU5F1B, yet the top CRC entry has T as the effect allele while other entries have G. This is not reconciled.

grades_final.reason: The TCF7L2 claim relies on CIS-BP-mapped LEF1/TCF7 models, which are only binding predictions. Their effects are small and the models rank low by |z|. The HCT116 TCF7L2 ChIP peak (E19) supports occupancy but not allelic preference. The direction (ref binds more) agrees across the passing models, so this is weak rather than missing.

The variant lies in a pELS cCRE with high DNase and H3K27ac (E03) and an Ensembl enhancer (E01). These are epigenomic maxima across biosamples, not HCT116-specific, and are context only, so the element link is only weakly supported.

MYC is chosen by distance and relevance. Open Targets gives MYC L2G 0.05 against POU5F1B 0.89, and no eQTL, Hi-C or CRISPR evidence links the element to MYC. The cited evidence does not support the claim, and the PVT1 sc-eQTL is only suggestive context.
The HCT116 ChIP peak shows TCF7L2 at the position in a colorectal line, which is context only. It does not show that the allele matters there, or that MYC is regulated in that cell type.

The CRC association is very strong (E04), but effect-allele reporting conflicts (T in the top entry, G in others) and the chain does not resolve this. The direction argument is unresolved, and E06a is only a GWAS replication quote with no mechanism.
The binding evidence is the same as in H1: related-factor CIS-BP predictions plus a TCF7L2 ChIP peak in HCT116. This is a weak prediction with no allele-specific data.
The variant lies in a pELS cCRE and in a CCAT2 exon (E01, E03), with SCREEN-linked genes including POU5F1B. This is epigenomic and annotation context only, so it is weak.

The GTEx colon eQTL (T raises POU5F1B, NES +0.20), L2G 0.89 and TWAS all point to POU5F1B, which is genetic support. However, no perturbation shows the element regulates POU5F1B, and the repressive role of TCF7L2 is not demonstrated. The eQTL is only a weak association (p 8e-6), and the TF-to-gene direction is inferred.

The eQTL is in transverse colon tissue and the ChIP is in HCT116. These are different systems, and co-occurrence of TF and eQTL does not establish that TF and target respond in the same cells. Only a loose tissue-level link is shown.

E06c shows POU5F1B promotes CRC proliferation, and the T-allele direction is consistent with the top GWAS entry. Conflicting G effect-allele entries are not reconciled, and no causal link from the variant to POU5F1B to phenotype is shown.

The ZBTB43 prediction is a QBiC in vitro own-model hit (ref preferred) with expression of 8.32 TPM. There is no occupancy or perturbation evidence. The chain itself admits ZBTB43 is not uniquely indicated, and the choice among ref-preferring hits is arbitrary.
The cCRE and enhancer context is generic. No evidence for ZBTB43 occupancy or a repressive role is cited, so only the element annotation is supported.

The POU5F1B eQTL, L2G and TWAS support the gene in general. However, the link between ZBTB43 binding loss and POU5F1B de-repression has no evidence, so the chain's gene link rests only on locus-level genetics.
The only evidence is expression of ZBTB43 in HCT116 and POU5F1B function in CRC cells. No ChIP places ZBTB43 at the element, so the cell-type link is weak.
POU5F1B promotes CRC growth, which is consistent with the T-allele association. Conflicting effect-allele entries are unreconciled, and nothing ties ZBTB43 to the phenotype.

G002 has an alt-preferring best model (NR2F6), but members disagree in direction. NR2F2 is not a passing member and was chosen only for being the most abundant, which is not a valid basis. This is a binding prediction alone for a TF that is not itself in coverage, and the chain's own text flags the weak basis.
The pELS cCRE is active by epigenomic maxima across biosamples. This is only generic context and nothing specific to a nuclear-receptor site is cited.
POU5F1B is supported by the eQTL and L2G, but the activator mechanism through an NR site is hypothetical. No evidence connects NR binding to POU5F1B expression.
Only expression of nuclear receptors in HCT116 is shown (E14). Occupancy is not shown, so this is expression context only.
POU5F1B promotes CRC growth, which fits the T-allele reading. No evidence links an NR site to the phenotype, and the conflicting G effect-allele entries are ignored here.
